newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan says won't levy tax on multimedia computers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan says won't levy tax on multimedia computers.

text.p: Taiwan's finance ministry said on Wednesday it has decided against imposing sales tax on multimedia computers.
The ministry had said earlier on Wednesday that multimedia computers should not enjoy their current tax exemption if the machines include standard outfits like CD-ROMs and speakers.
"But we decided that the extra outfits are simply attachments to the computer and therefore cannot be taxed as actual products," vice finance minister Yen Ching-chang told reporters.

The ministry had said it may tax multimedia computers according to the rate of 10-13 percent currently imposed on electronic products like stereo and television sets because the computers also serve those functions.
"But our conclusion is that no one would buy a computer for its function as a television or a stereo, because you can easily get better televisions or stereos for cheaper," Yen said.
"So it doesn't make sense to tax computers as if they are electronic products," he added.
The local Economic Daily News said on Wednesday that profits for computer makers would fall and retail prices for computers would soar if multimedia computers were levied with a sales tax.
